articles.title: Kiri and Lou Go Raaa! review – delightful origin story for CBeebies’ prehistoric pals
articles.summary: The pair’s first feature-length adventure stars Jemaine Clement and Olivia Tennet, has a dreamy soundtrack and beautiful stop-motion visuals – fantastic family fun. Kiri is a lively yellow dinosaur, Lou is an amiable purple palorchecie (a fictional beast, vaguely resembling a palorchestes, which in…
body: At only one hour long, the runtime is toddler-friendly – and to be honest, there are plenty of films marketed at adults that could learn a lesson from writer-director Harry Sinclair’s economical storytelling. (Sinclair is also the writer of the TV series, alongside Buffy the Vampire Slayer writing alum Rebecca Kirshner.) With the voice acting talents of Olivia Tennet (Freda in Lord of the Rings: The Two Towers) and Jemaine Clement (Flight of the Conchords), plus dreamy songs from Don McGlashan (Blam Blam Blam, The Front Lawn), Kiri and Lou Go Raaa! would arguably work superbly as an audiobook or radio show – except the visuals are a treat too.

articles.title: Russell T Davies Calls BBC Boss’ AI ‘Doctor Who’ Comment ‘Clumsy’ and Teases Show’s Future: ‘You’ll Start to See Production’ in ‘Summer Next Year’
articles.summary: Outgoing “Doctor Who” showrunner Russell T. Davies has criticised BBC director general Matt Brittin over recent comments he made regarding an AI-generated episode of the cult show.
body: Davies — who revived “Doctor Who” in 2005 and then returned again in 2023 — also said that Brittin, who only recently joined the BBC following a career at Google, “hasn’t worked in television for that long and might not be so fruity with an opinion in future.”

The future of “Doctor Who” — a BBC icon for more than 60 years — is currently up in the air following the departure of Disney+ as a co-financier. This summer, Davies announced he would be stepping back and the BBC cancelled the planned Christmas special. Last month, the BBC launched a competitive tender inviting pitches from producers to reboot the series. “Line of Duty” creator Jed Mercurio is among those to have submitted their interest.
But while fans wait to see what happens, Davies, despite no longer being involved in the show, assured that a new series was definitely happening and there wouldn’t be too long to wait.
“You’ll start to see production with a brand-new Doctor, a brand-new companion, summer next year,” he said.

articles.title: Philippine-Italian Sales Alliance Targets Indie Film Buyers in Asia, Europe and North America (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: A new Philippine-Italian sales alliance aims to put independent films in front of buyers in Asia, Europe and North America. Fire & Ice Media, the Philippine producer and sales agent, and Italy’s Coccinelle Film Sales unveiled the strategic partnership at Busan’s Asian Contents & Film Market.
body: The pair will work together on a handpicked group of films, combining their regional know-how and buyer contacts to seek distribution deals beyond the films’ home markets. A first batch of films has already been chosen, though the companies have yet to name them.

“Every film has its own audience and its own potential in different markets. Our job is to understand where those opportunities are and work with the right people to make them happen,” said Diño-Cabrera. “Partnering with Coccinelle allows us to strengthen our reach, share market knowledge, and create more possibilities for the filmmakers and producers who trust us to represent their work.”

Coccinelle, set up by Francesca Breccia, sells independent titles on the international circuit, pairing films and their rights owners with buyers and distributors in a range of territories. Breccia said the company already had sales alliances with Asian counterparts, notably in South Korea and Thailand, and was delighted to now bring the Philippines into that network.

articles.title: Tallinn-Bound Indian Drama ‘Kidney’ Boarded by Shiladitya Bora’s Platoon One Films (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Indian drama “Kidney,” the second feature from filmmaking siblings Aakarsh and Agrim Sansanwal, has been boarded by Shiladitya Bora’s Platoon One Films, which joins as co-producer ahead of the film’s slot in the Critics’ Picks Competition at Estonia’s Tallinn Black Nights Film Festival (PÖFF).
body: “Kidney” adds to a Platoon One slate that counts “Bayaan,” “Toh Ti Ani Fuji,” “Bhagwan Bharose,” “Minimum,” “Ghaath,” “Picasso” and “Yours Truly” among its titles.

The director said Platoon One was among the first to spot that spirit in the film and back what the brothers were attempting. “Their support gave the film a chance to travel beyond the world in which it was made and reach audiences we could only have hoped for. To see it now receive recognition and find its way into the light is deeply moving. My thanks to the Tallinn Black Nights team for discovering our film and giving it a place to shine.”

Tallinn’s Critics’ Picks strand spotlights films with a clear artistic point of view and a fresh take on storytelling, including work that wrestles with genre, cinema’s past and the social issues of the moment. Earlier selections include Arati Kadav’s “Mrs.,” starring Sanya Malhotra, as well as “The Brothers Kitaura,” “About Us But Not About Us” and “The Bone Breakers.”

articles.title: Wuthering Heights: The House of the Damned review – Brontë horror do-over is part Dracula, part Jeeves and Wooster
articles.summary: Emily Brontë’s classic is reimagined with extra stranglings, slashings and pitchfork impalings but plays it straight. Where pornography once trod, horror has now become the genre that infiltrates and apes all others.
body: Hirani puts undeniable effort in getting her plot points to line up with Brontë’s – even if most of the characters, including poor old Lockwood’s horse, meet a much grislier fate. Rationed out in snippets of Catherine’s diary, the confidences of housekeeper Nelly (Nicola Wright) and more random supernatural flashbacks involving Lockwood, the manor’s backstory is rather garbled, though with the OTT hook of Heathcliff as an 18th-century Yorkshire Ripper. Rather than amping up the camp, as the likes of Kate Bush and Emerald Fennell did in their takes on the novel, Hirani plays it straight and dour, mystifyingly so, given the extra stranglings, slashings and pitchfork-impalings she’s chucked in.

articles.title: Frank and Percy review – bromance becomes romance for dog walkers Ian McKellen and Roger Allam
articles.summary: London film festival McKellen and Allam reprise their roles for the film version of Ben Weatherill’s play in a star-filled bittersweet comedy about finding love later in life.
body: Allam plays Frank, a retired history teacher whose wife died of cancer a few short years ago (Belinda is his sister-in-law) and who now likes to walk his dog Toffee on Hampstead Heath. McKellen is Percy, an academic sociologist and climate scientist who can be found there too, with his dog Bruno. Percy is rather acrimoniously separated from his now ex-partner, a waspish and querulously self-pitying figure gamely played by Stephen Fry.

This leads Frank to ponder if he is bisexual – but perhaps it is more that he is simply sexual, and sexual in a way that he never expected to be at this time of life, or any time of life, and could only have been with this individual person. We get some bittersweet comedy as Frank and Percy realise that their social life consists of funerals, and Percy has a startling Yorick moment looking at the churchyard’s headstones. “Oh my God! I’ve had him!”

Naturally, the course of true love, or any sort of love, does not run smooth and at one stage Belinda, in a moment of lucidity, tells Frank: “How lucky you are to have a broken heart at 77!” True enough. It’s a love story as comforting as the cups of tea and slices of cake to which the characters are partial.

articles.title: Look North sofa to be pushed 80 miles for Children in Need
articles.summary: Lindsey Burrow and Amy Garcia will travel 80 miles across Yorkshire.
body: The wife of rugby league legend Rob Burrow will join BBC Look North presenter Amy Garcia for this year's Children in Need charity challenge.
Lindsey Burrow and Amy plan to push the programme's red sofa 80 miles (129km) across Yorkshire over five days, covering 12-20 miles each day.

The pair will start at Ripon on Monday 9 November and pass through South Yorkshire before crossing the finish line in Wakefield on Friday 13 November. Their efforts will be broadcast live along the route.
Last year, they raised tens of thousands of pounds on a three-legged walk for BBC Children in Need.

articles.title: Ian McKellen set to perform as a hologram in new play
articles.summary: The Lord of the Rings actor stars in An Ark which will have its European premier in Manchester.
body: Sir Ian McKellen is set to star in the European premier of a play in which he appears as a hologram.
The 87-year-old Lord of the Rings star, who was born in Burnley, will perform in An Ark when it comes to Manchester's Factory International Aviva Studios.
The play, which debuted in New York, will feature McKellen and Bridgerton star Golda Rosheuvel in 3D holographic form, which was achieved using 52 cameras filming them from multiple angles.
McKellen said: "A new Simon Stephens play is always an excitement but when it is written to be performed in this unique way, it feels more like an explosion."

articles.title: Netflix unveils first trailer for Greta Gerwig’s Narnia: The Magician’s Nephew
articles.summary: The fantasy epic based on CS Lewis’s classic stars Daniel Craig, Carey Mulligan and Meryl Streep. The first look at Greta Gerwig ’s vision for Narnia has been revealed.
body: Today, Netflix is giving a first look at her vision for CS Lewis ’s magical world in the trailer for The Magician’s Nephew, the first chronological book in the beloved series.

With the soundtrack of Led Zeppelin’s Stairway to Heaven, the trailer opens with magician Andrew Ketterley ( Daniel Craig ) intoning that “sometimes one story is the beginning to all the others”, as he gives a group of kids a magic ring that will transport them to strange and wonderful lands.
Elsewhere, the trailer gives a first look at many locations and characters familiar to fans, including Jadis (Emma Mackey, the future White Witch) and Aslan, the mythical lion voiced by Meryl Streep.

The Magician’s Nephew tells the story of two children in Edwardian England named Digory and Polly (newcomers David McKenna and Beatrice Campbell) who chance upon the Wood Between Worlds, a realm with many portals to different dimensions. There, they witness the birth of Narnia.

articles.title: Russell T Davies criticises BBC boss's 'clumsy' AI Doctor Who comments
articles.summary: BBC director general Matt Brittin said he had seen a "pretty good" AI-generated episode of the show.
body: Longtime Doctor Who writer and showrunner Russell T Davies has criticised the new BBC director general over comments he made about an AI-generated episode of the show.
Matt Brittin told a Royal Television Society conference in September that he had been sent a "pretty good" 50-minute unofficial Doctor Who episode.
"That's a clumsy thing to say in an industry where he's got writers and artists and it specifically affects people, they're the first to take the blow," Davies told BBC Radio 4's The Media Show.
Addressing criticism he has received, Brittin told a staff meeting last week he was attempting to make a point around the "pace of change" while stressing he believed in "human creativity".
